name.text: Alternate Segment Theorem - Solve for x (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
In the figure, \(PT\) is a tangent to the circle at \(T\), \(TQ\) is a chord, and \(S\) lies in the alternate segment. The marked angles are

\[ \angle PTQ = ({@e1@})^\circ \qquad\text{and}\qquad \angle TSQ = ({@e2@})^\circ . \] [[jsxgraph width="470px" height="470px"]] var A = {#taA#}; var a1 = {#a1#}, b1 = {#b1#}; var a2 = {#a2#}, b2 = {#b2#}; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-3.4, 3.2, 3.4, -3.4], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); var R = 2.5; var rad = Math.PI / 180; var aT = 270; function lin(a, b) { var s = a + 'x'; if (b > 0) s += ' + ' + b; else if (b < 0) s += ' - ' + (-b); return '(' + s + ')°'; } var O = board.create('point', [0, 0], {visible: false, fixed: true}); board.create('circle', [O, R], {strokeColor: '#888', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); var T = board.create('point', [R * Math.cos(aT * rad), R * Math.sin(aT * rad)], {name: 'T', size: 3, fixed: true, fillColor: '#1565c0', strokeColor: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [0, -14], anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top'}}); var Q = board.create('point', [R * Math.cos((aT + 2 * A) * rad), R * Math.sin((aT + 2 * A) * rad)], {name: 'Q', size: 3, fixed: true, fillColor: '#1565c0', strokeColor: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [12, 2], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle'}}); var S = board.create('point', [R * Math.cos((90 + A) * rad), R * Math.sin((90 + A) * rad)], {name: 'S', size: 3, fixed: true, fillColor: '#1565c0', strokeColor: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [-12, 2], anchorX: 'right', anchorY: 'middle'}}); var Ty = R * Math.sin(aT * rad); var Lend = board.create('point', [-2.0, Ty], {visible: false, fixed: true}); var P = board.create('point', [2.0, Ty], {name: 'P', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [6, -2], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle'}}); board.create('segment', [Lend, P], {strokeColor: '#333', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [T, Q], {strokeColor: '#333', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [T, S], {strokeColor: '#333', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); board.create('segment', [S, Q], {strokeColor: '#333', strokeWidth: 1.5, fixed: true}); board.create('angle', [P, T, Q], {radius: 0.7, type: 'sector', selection: 'minor', fillColor: '#90caf9', fillOpacity: 0.5, strokeColor: '#1565c0', name: lin(a1, b1), fixed: true}); board.create('angle', [T, S, Q], {radius: 0.6, type: 'sector', selection: 'minor', fillColor: '#c5e1a5', fillOpacity: 0.5, strokeColor: '#558b2f', name: lin(a2, b2), fixed: true}); [[/jsxgraph]]
(a) Find \( x = \) [[input:ans1]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]
(b) Hence find \( \angle PTQ = \) [[input:ans2]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
By the Alternate Segment Theorem, the tangent-chord angle equals the inscribed angle in the alternate segment, so \( \angle PTQ = \angle TSQ \):

\[ {@e1@} \;=\; {@e2@}. \]

Collecting terms gives \( {@a1-a2@}\,x = {@b2-b1@} \), so

\[ x = {@taX@}. \]

(b) Substituting back,

\[ \angle PTQ = ({@e1@}) = ({@a1@}\times {@taX@} + {@b1@})^\circ = {@taA@}^\circ , \]

and as a check \( \angle TSQ = {@taA@}^\circ \) too.

falsefeedback.text: Set the two marked angles equal (not supplementary): \( \angle PTQ = \angle TSQ \) by the Alternate Segment Theorem. Then collect the \(x\) terms and solve the linear equation. See the worked solution.
